previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, and recurrent UTIs was admitted for hyperglycemia and a persistent dry cough. She was found to be in mild diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 406 and an anion gap of 16, along with acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.9). She was treated with IV fluids and an insulin drip, then transitioned back to her insulin pump with adjusted basal rates. Her kidney function improved (creatinine 1.1) and DKA resolved. Evaluation for infection included a negative CT chest for pneumonia, negative respiratory viral panel, and negative urine Legionella antigen. Her chronic cough and eye discomfort were attributed to allergic rhinitis, likely triggered by environmental factors, and she was started on Nasacort nasal spray. She remained on her baseline immunosuppressive and chronic medications, with stable cyclosporine levels. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up labs and primary care appointments.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma
Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
